[kimi @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6] verdict=fail; failed checks: source_identity, completeness, negation, agency, modality, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [source_identity] ""Cease from your wicked deeds" (Isaiah 1:16)" vs "Παύσασθε ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν": No Isaiah 1:16 citation in source; verse reference invented by translator.; [completeness] "missing: καὶ πάντων κρατεῖ" vs "ἣ μὴ μόνου τοῦ ἡγιασμένου γένους ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντων κρατεῖ": Dropped clause 'but all things it rules'—source says authority rules all things, not just 'all things' as adjectival.; [agency] "It is allegorized as God's footstool" vs "ὑποπόδιον ἀλληγορουμένη θεοῦ": Subject is 'authority' (feminine ἐξουσίαν), not 'it' neuter; feminine participle ἀλληγορουμένη agrees with authority, not footstool.; [completeness] "occupying the whole inhabited earth" vs "τὴν πᾶσαν ἐπέχον γῆν οἰκουμένην": Missing 'being called footstool by same name'—participle ἐπέχον and following ὁμωνύμως...καλουμένην not fully rendered as connected clause.; [negation] "which rules not only the sanctified race but all things" vs "ἣ μὴ μόνου τοῦ ἡγιασμένου γένους ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντων κρατεῖ": μὴ μόνου...ἀλλὰ καὶ = 'not only...but also'; translator drops 'also', weakening the not-only-but-also construction.; [completeness] "The throne that is above the authority" vs "ὁ ὑπὲρ τὴν ἐξουσίαν ὢν θρόνος": ὢν 'being' participle omitted; 'that is above' adds relative not in source structure.; [modality] "would be allegorized" vs "δ' ἂν ἀλληγοροῖτο": ἂν with optative = potential 'would be', but δέ marks this as continuing same allegorical method, not a new hypothetical.; [completeness] "above all with the heavenly things, but already also with the things on earth" vs "μάλιστα μὲν πρὸς τὰ οὐράνια, ἤδη δὲ καὶ πρὸς τὰ ἐν γῇ": μάλιστα μὲν = 'most of all' or 'especially', not merely 'above all'; μέν...δέ correlation weakened.; [completeness] "in the manner of heaven" vs "ἐν τῷ οὐρανοῦ τρόπῳ": τρόπῳ = 'manner' but genitive οὐρανοῦ = 'of heaven'; 'in the manner of heaven' acceptable but 'heavenly manner' closer.; [completeness] "since we say that Jerusalem, a small part of the earth, is a throne" vs "ὁπότε θρόνον καὶ Ἱερουσαλὴμ τὸ βραχὺ γῆς μέρος...φαμέν": ὁπότε = 'when' not 'since'; causal 'since' changes logical relation to temporal 'when'.; [completeness] "and that the authority set over those who are ruled is a footstool" vs "ὑποπόδιον δὲ τὴν ἐποῦσαν τοῖς ἐξουσιαζομένοις ἐξουσίαν φαμέν": ἐποῦσαν = 'being over' or 'set over', but ἐξουσιαζομένοις = 'being ruled' passive; 'those who are ruled' correct but 'authority set over' adds 'set' not in source. | part 2/5: [source_identity] ""good seed," by the same name" vs "σπέρμα καλῶν ὁμωνύμως": Greek has "seed of good things" not "good seed"; misidentifies what is named; [agency] "he rightly removes" vs "τὸ εἰκότως ἀναιρεῖν": Infinitive with article is abstract 'the fittingly to-remove', not 'he removes'; [scripture] "(Psalm 98:9)" vs "Ps 98,9": LXX Ps 98:9 = Heb/Eng Ps 99:9, not 98:9; number should be [99:9]; [scripture] "(Psalm 100:8)" vs "Ps 100,8": LXX Ps 100:8 = Heb/Eng Ps 101:8, not 100:8; number should be [101:8]; [completeness] "The removal of the wicked is lawful" vs "νόμιμος δὲ ἡ τῶν πονηρῶν ἐξαίρεσις": Missing 'and' (δὲ) connecting to prior; breaks syntactic continuity | part 3/5: [source_identity] "(Psalm 101:3)" vs "170 Ps 101,3": Psalm 101:3 in LXX is Hebrew Psalm 102:3; English should note LXX numbering; [completeness] "he asks not to be overlooked by God" vs "τὸ μὴ περιοφθῆναι ὑπὸ θεοῦ": Missing 'the not to-be-overlooked' as noun phrase; 'he asks' is added subject/verb not in source; [agency] "the one speaking says in his own person what belongs to all" vs "τὸ λέγον πρόσωπον ἐφ' ἑαυτοῦ λέγει τὰ πάντων": 'what belongs to all' misrepresents τὰ πάντων 'the things of all' i.e. everyone's concerns; [modality] "he speaks also of the long affliction" vs "ἔτι δὲ καὶ τὴν ἐν μακρῷ χρόνῳ κάκωσιν": Missing finite verb; 'he speaks' supplied but source has accusative object continuing 'says'; [scripture] "(Psalm 101:14)" vs "171 ps 101,14": Psalm 101:14 in LXX is Hebrew Psalm 102:14; English should note LXX numbering; [negation] "not by any other cause" vs "οὐκ ἄλλη τις αἰτία": Correctly negated; no error; [completeness] "when the Savior came" vs "ἐπιδημήσαντος τοῦ σωτῆρος": 'having-come' is genitive absolute; 'when' acceptable, but 'came' loses participial syntax; [modality] "the Savior's descent also took place" vs "ἡ τοῦ σωτῆρος κάθοδος γέγονεν": 'took place' for γέγονεν acceptable; no major error | part 4/5: [source_identity] "For in the proper sense the Savior's descent also took place when he shone forth at the consummation of the ages." vs "ἐπεὶ γὰρ ἆραι τὴν ἁμαρτίαν τοῦ κόσμου ἐλήλυθεν ὁ σωτήρ": Invented clause not in Greek; no 'descent,' 'shone forth,' or 'consummation of the ages' in source.; [agency] "the law given through Moses also spoke against wickedness" vs "ἀπειπόντος δὲ πρὸς τὴν κακίαν καὶ νόμου τοῦ διὰ Μωυσέως δοθέντος": Wrong subject: participle ἀπειπόντος modifies patriarchs, not law; law is genitive, not nominative.; [modality] "God, who provides for their salvation, had to hinder the wickedness" vs "ἔδει τὸν προνοούμενον τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν θεὸν κωλῦσαι τὴν κακίαν": ἔδει = 'it was necessary,' not 'had to' with God as compelled subject; impersonal construction softened.; [completeness] "yet they despised the God who had given it" vs "αὐτοὶ μὲν κατεφρόνουν τοῦ δεδωκότος θεοῦ": Dropped αὐτοὶ μὲν 'they on their part' contrastive emphasis with following δέ clause. | part 5/5: [negation] "nothing more came of it" vs "οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἐγίνετο": Greek says 'nothing rather/more came-to-be' not 'nothing more came of it'; [agency] "they were worn down" vs "ἐπετρίβοντο": Middle/passive ambiguous; 'worn down' obscures they wore themselves down; [completeness] "brought to them" vs "προσαγόμενον": dative of advantage 'to them' not in Greek; participle lacks expressed object
[glm @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2] verdict=fail; failed checks: completeness, scripture; uncertainties: 0; model notes: part 1/5: [scripture] "“Cease from your wicked deeds” (Isaiah 1:16)." vs "τοῦτο νομίζοντες ἐκείνῳ τῷ Παύσασθε ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν.": Source has no Scripture reference; translator inserts '(Isaiah 1:16)' not in the Greek text. | part 2/5: [completeness] "he attacks the falsely named gods, who are not holy" vs "τῶν οὐχ ἁγίων κατατρέχει ψευδωνύμων θεῶν": Drops the article-noun phrase 'τῶν οὐχ ἁγίων' which is the object of κατατρέχει; 'who are not holy' is a relative gloss, not the Greek.; [scripture] ""Remove the wicked one from among yourselves" (1 Corinthians 5:13; cf. Deuteronomy 17:7)." vs "Ἐξαιρεῖτε τὸν πονηρὸν ἐξ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν.": Source has no cross-reference; the LXX phrase matches Deut 17:7, not 1 Cor 5:13 which reads ἐξάρατε.
Latin quote (from model note, verified): «Παύσασθε ἀπὸ τῶν πονηριῶν ὑμῶν»
English quote (from model note, verified): «Cease from your wicked deeds»
ADJUDICATED @cf/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (Densify (agent), direct clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Checked every flag against the Greek; none is a meaning error. Bible references in parentheses (Isaiah 1:16, 1 Corinthians 5:13 / Deuteronomy 17:7, Isaiah 49:8, 2 Corinthians 6:2, Romans 3:23, Hebrews 2:9) are identification apparatus for words the Greek quotes. Psalm numbers are the edition's own LXX fragment headings (Ps 98,5bc; 100,8; 101,3; 101,14), used throughout this work. 'For in the proper sense the Savior's descent also took place when he shone forth at the consummation of the ages' renders κυρίως γὰρ καὶ ἡ τοῦ σωτῆρος κάθοδος γέγονεν ἐπιλάμψαντος ἐπὶ συντελείᾳ τῶν αἰώνων (present in the source; the chunk split put it in the previous part). ἀπειπόντος … νόμου τοῦ διὰ Μωυσέως δοθέντος is a genitive absolute with the law as subject ('the law given through Moses also spoke against wickedness'), as rendered. καλεῖ σπέρμα καλῶν ὁμωνύμως keeps the homonymy (Matt 13:38: the good seed are the children of the kingdom). οὐδὲν μᾶλλον ἐγίνετο, ἢ εἰς αὔξησιν κακίας ἐπετρίβοντο: 'nothing more came of it: they were worn down into an increase of wickedness' keeps the sense that things only got worse. The rest (articular infinitives, μέν/δέ, ὤν, ἄν + optative, feminine agreement with ἐξουσία) are syntax and style, rendered correctly in sense.
ADJUDICATED @cf/zai-org/glm-5.2 (Densify (agent), direct clause check against the Greek, 2026-10-09): Not meaning errors. (Isaiah 1:16) and (1 Corinthians 5:13; cf. Deuteronomy 17:7) identify words the Greek quotes; Ἐξαιρεῖτε (imperative plural) is closest to 1 Cor 5:13 ἐξάρατε, with Deut 17:7 LXX as its source, so both are given. 'he attacks the falsely named gods, who are not holy' renders τῶν οὐχ ἁγίων κατατρέχει ψευδωνύμων θεῶν; 'not holy' is kept. GLM's previous run flagged 'as when … he says' for ὥσπερ θεὸς … δηλῶν Ὀρθρίζων φησὶν ἀποστέλλων; that was corrected before this gate to 'just as God, showing that he sends the prophets with zeal, says'. Chunks 3, 4 and 5 pass.
